headline: High Court Clerk Demands Replacement Of Presiding Judge For Using 'Questionable' Font In Daily Cause List
body:
Q: Mr. Chatterjee, you’ve filed a formal request to replace the sitting judge. Is this due to a procedural disagreement or a legal conflict?

A: It’s purely aesthetic, frankly. His Honor insists on using Comic Sans for all official trial listings. How can the gravity of the law be maintained when the accused is being summoned to a hearing in a font that looks like it belongs on a child’s lemonade stand menu?

Q: Surely the font doesn't interfere with the administration of justice?

A: When you open the cause list and the words 'Life Imprisonment' are dancing at you in bubbly, rounded letters, the entire courtroom loses its focus. I’ve requested the Chief Justice step in. Either we switch to the professional sanctity of Times New Roman, or we find a judge who understands that the majesty of the bar isn't a nursery school art project.
caption: Law and order depends on the typeface. Apparently, the court’s hierarchy is currently being held hostage by a font choice that has no business appearing in a legal document. #LegalDrama #FontWars #JusticeSystem (satire)
igHook: Would you take a court summons seriously if it were written in Comic Sans?
